claims.text: An integrated high-throughput computational and experimental workflow can identify refractory HEA compositions that combine intrinsic strength, ductility, and low weight.
The proposed computational workflow combines first-principles thermo-kinetic analysis, CALPHAD modeling, and machine learning.
Optimizing phase stability and beneficial lattice distortions enables the targeted combination of strength, ductility, and low weight.
A multi-principal mixture of refractory elements such as W, Ta, V, and Cr can form a single-phase refractory HEA.
The initial refractory alloy is a disordered solid solution.
Machine-learning-aided first-principles and CALPHAD screening can narrow the refractory HEA composition space.
Magnetron sputtering can be used to synthesize W-Ta-V-Cr refractory HEA films for experimental characterization.
Room-temperature magnetron sputtering can produce a single-phase BCC W-Ta-V-Cr alloy.
The designed alloy has engineered atomic-scale lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion creates a rough energy landscape that controls defect-recombination kinetics.
The alloy contains nanocrystalline regions and consequently has high grain-boundary density.
Optimized elemental ratios produce nearly equal vacancy and interstitial mobilities.
Nearly equal vacancy and interstitial mobilities reduce defect clustering.
Optimized elemental ratios balance bonding strengths.
Optimized elemental ratios lower the overall alloy density.
Reduced defect clustering, balanced bonding strengths, and lower density jointly cause high strength, improved ductility, and reduced mass.
The resulting refractory HEA will be predominantly single-phase and nanocrystalline.
The resulting alloy will have greater strength and ductility and lower density than conventionally designed refractory alloys.
Traditional empirical or sequential design typically requires multiple iterations to balance strength, ductility, and weight.
Variability in synthesis methods and scale-up challenges makes the degree of property improvement uncertain.
